fact_checks: The verified facts confirm security.accesscondition.composes.security.policyrule exists, and composes is the only predicate from accesscondition to policyrule.
The opposite direction, policyrule -> accesscondition, already carries a uses relationship, so the proposed fallback ('drop it in favor of uses') targets an existing edge.

The facts define composes as a whole-part relationship where the part cannot exist without the whole, but they do not say whether source or target is the whole, so the claimed reversal depends on unstated convention.

The current schema says accesscondition is 'composed inside a PolicyRule condition chain', which makes policyrule the whole. The proposed definition also places accesscondition in ResourceOperation and InformationRight, so it can exist outside any policyrule.

arguments_for: If the spec reads composes as source-is-whole, as ArchiMate composition does, this edge makes accesscondition the whole, contradicting the schema text 'composed inside a PolicyRule'.
Pairing policyrule-uses-accesscondition with accesscondition-composes-policyrule gives contradictory or redundant semantics for one pair, which confuses modellers and CLI validation.
Composition says the part cannot exist without the whole, but the proposed definition lets accesscondition live in ResourceOperation and InformationRight checks too.
arguments_against: The facts do not state the composes direction convention; English 'conditions compose a rule' reads naturally as part-to-whole, so the edge may already be correct.
Reversing the edge without first checking how other composes relationships across layers are oriented risks introducing inconsistency rather than fixing it.

arguments_for: If the spec reads 'A composes B' as 'A is a part composing B', the edge says access conditions compose policy rules, which matches the schema description.
The existing reverse 'uses' edge lets policyrule reference conditions, while composes expresses the part side. That pairing may be intentional rather than an error.
arguments_against: The proposed definition says accesscondition also sits within ResourceOperation and InformationRight, which undermines the 'cannot exist without the whole' meaning of composes.
Even if the direction is intended, having both composes and uses between the same pair suggests the design was not deliberately reconciled.

arguments_for: Choosing between composes, uses, or both depends on whether accesscondition is reusable across rules and other elements. That is a modelling decision, not an objective error.
The claimant offers two alternatives, reversing or dropping, which signals that more than one reasonable resolution exists.
Whether the predicate's direction convention is source-whole or source-part is a spec-wide choice needing a product decision.
arguments_against: The direction convention for composes should already be fixed spec-wide; if it is, the edge is either right or wrong, not a matter of taste.
Leaving contradictory composes and uses edges unresolved has concrete costs for CLI validation, which argues for treating this as a correction.

arguments_for: One could argue that how the CLI renders relationship direction is a tooling concern.
arguments_against: The claim targets a specific relationship defined in the security layer schema, which is squarely spec content.
Relationships between policyrule and accesscondition are core to the XACML-style policy modelling the layer intent names explicitly.
